Subject: Order form invoicing: initial questions on invoice routing and tax residency

Hi Taylor —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Two quick items from procurement as we prep the final Order Form:

1) Invoice recipient: they asked that invoices be issued to “Acme Therapeutics Inc.” (US entity) — please confirm the exact legal name and remit-to address we should use on the invoice.
2) Tax/residency evidence: procurement flagged that they may require a tax residency certificate and want to understand whether Redwood will apply any gross-up or withholding on our invoices.
3) Net terms: Acme has asked for Net 45 in the PO; our standard commercial asks Net 30. If Net 45 is necessary we need to route to finance for approval.

Can you confirm the preferred invoice recipient and whether Acme will provide tax residency docs? I can loop in our finance/legal to lock the wording in the Order Form.

Appreciate it —
Jordan Blake
Commercial Ops | Redwood Inference

Thanks for the note. Confirming details from our side:

- Legal invoicing name: Acme Therapeutics, Inc.
- Remit-to: 1800 Commerce Rd, Suite 400, Boston, MA 02110

- Tax residency: we can provide a US tax residency letter (we use that for vendor onboarding). I attached the PO (PO_4532.pdf) to this reply.

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order form invoicing: initial questions on invoice routing and tax residency

Jordan / Karthik —

Thanks for forwarding Taylor’s reply and the PO. Quick internal guidance from Finance/Legal: 

- Invoice recipient: we should mirror exactly what Acme confirmed (Acme Therapeutics, Inc.). Add a one-line field in the Order Form called “Invoice Recipient (legal name)” to capture this and avoid manual rework.
- Net terms: our standard is Net 30. Approve Net 45 only for deals > $300k ARR or with Finance sponsorship. This deal is below that threshold; recommend we hold on Net 45 and propose Net 30. If Acme pushes, we can escalate to Commercial Leadership.
- Tax/residency and withholding: Redwood will not gross-up unless contractually required. For US customers, we will request a tax residency certificate (Tax_Cert_Acme.pdf stub) and collect W-9 if needed. If the invoice is routed to a non-US entity in the future, we will follow country-specific withholding rules and will need supporting documentation (e.g., EU reverse-charge evidence).
- Consolidated invoicing / netting: Redwood supports consolidated monthly statements for customers that have an entity mapping set up in our billing system. For first-time customers we typically invoice the legal entity that signs the Order Form. If Acme wants consolidated billing across multiple entities, this requires an entity mapping task and an Ops ticket before go-live.

Action items I suggest we include in the thread: 
- Jordan to confirm preferred net terms with Acme (propose Net 30).
- Jordan to request tax residency/W-9 from Acme (procurement to attach).
- Kimberly to attach standard invoice-routing appendix to the Order Form and flag if Net 45 approval is required.

Attaching internal playbook for routing: invoice-routing-playbook.docx

-Kimberly
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Taylor —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the PO. Per our internal review here’s the proposed path so we can finalize the Order Form today: 

Summary / plan
- Invoice recipient: Redwood will issue invoices to “Acme Therapeutics, Inc.” at the remit-to address you provided.
- Net terms: We propose Net 30. If Acme requires Net 45, please let us know and we will flag for Finance approval; otherwise we will issue Net 30 on the Order Form.
- Tax documents: Please attach your tax residency letter and W-9 (if available) to the reply. We’ll hold invoicing until we receive the W-9/tax residency doc.
- Consolidated billing: For this initial implementation we will invoice the signing legal entity only. If you require consolidated monthly statements across entities, we can set that up but it will require an entity mapping task and Ops lead time (~2–4 weeks).

Next steps / asks from Acme
- Confirm whether Net 30 is acceptable or confirm the push for Net 45 (so we can escalate if required).
- Upload the tax residency letter + W-9 to this thread or send to kimberly_park@redwood.com.

I’ve attached a near-final Order Form (Redwood_OrderForm_v2.pdf) that includes a short invoice-routing appendix (redline-ready). If you’re good with Net 30 and will provide the tax docs, I’ll send for signature and route the first invoice to the address you provided. DocuSign link is included below when we’re ready.
